SECOND, SEPARATE FRAGILITY ON THE SAME PATH: `covered.add((gate.name, env_name))` runs BEFORE that guard while `readings.setdefault(...)` runs after it, so even if the guard were fixed to catch LeverError, the census loop's `elif len(readings[(gate_name, env_name)]) < 2` would then raise KeyError for the same pair. Both need fixing together. findings.detail:
F8's own docstring calls REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD a first-class configuration and quotes D4 ('make OFF a first-class configuration'), and it has an arm asserting what OFF must return (Windows(-5), the pre-refusal behaviour). That arm is satisfied. But flipping the switch to False and changing NOTHING else still turns F8 RED -- on the joint-naming assertion, because FAB.manage_period is the only layer on the path that names the lever beside the value it read, and with the switch off it does not refuse at all, leaving only the assembly's refusal, which names the value but not the lever adjacent to it.
